channel.description: Recent content in dict on ThingsDB documentation

item.title: clear
item.description: Removes all items from a dict. This function generates a change Function dict.clear() Arguments None Return value Returns nil. Example This code adds things to a set: d = dict(range(10).map(|i| [uuid(), i])); assert( d.len() == 10 ); // dict with 10 items d.clear(); assert( d.len() == 0 ); // the dict is empty d; Return value in JSON format []

item.title: copy
item.description: Copy a dict. If a deep value higher than 0 (default) is used, then this function will create copies of the potential things within the dict values. This function does not generate a change. Function dict.copy([deep]]) Arguments Argument Type Description deep int (optional) How deep to copy things withing the dict. Default is 0 (only a copy of the dict, not the potential things within the dict values).

item.title: del
item.description: Delete a item from a dict by its key. This function generates a change. Function dict.del(key) Arguments Argument Type Description key str/int/uuid (required) Key for the item to delete. Return value Returns the removed value if successful. A lookup_err() is returned if the key does not exist. Example This code shows some return values for del(): d = dict([[123, 'Hello ThingsDB!

item.title: dup
item.description: Duplicate a dict. If a deep value higher than 0 (default) is used, then this function will also create duplicates of the things within the dict. This function does not generate a change. Function dict.dup([deep]]) Arguments Argument Type Description deep int (optional) How deep to duplicate things withing the dict. Default is 0 (only a duplicate of the dict, not the things within the dict).

item.title: each
item.description: Iterate over items in a dict. Be aware that the order when iterating over a dict, dict or a thing is not guaranteed. This function does not generate a change. Function dict.each(callback) Arguments Argument Type Description callback closure (required) Closure to execute on each value. Explanation of the callback argument: Iterable Arguments Description dict key, value Iterate over items in the dict.

item.title: get
item.description: Return the value of a item in a dict by a given key. If the key is not found then the return value will be nil, unless an alternative return value is given. This function does not generate a change. Function dict.get(name, [alt]) Arguments Argument Type Description name uuid/int/str (required) The key where to return the value for. alt any (optional) Optional return value.

item.title: has
item.description: Determines if a given key exists in a dict. This function does not generate a change. Function dict.has(key) Arguments Argument Type Description key uuid/int/str (required) Key to check. Return value Returns true if the given key is found in the dict and otherwise false. Example This code shows an example use case of has(): d = dict([[42, "The answer to everything"]]); /* Check if the dict has a key 42 */ d.

item.title: keys
item.description: Returns a list containing all the keys of the dict. The order of keys in the list is not guaranteed and may be different each time you run the query. This function does not generate a change. Function dict.keys() Arguments None Return value Returns a list with the keys of a dict. Example This code shows how to use keys(): dict([ [uuid("00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"), 'UUIDs can be used as keys'], [-1, 'Integer keys can be negative'], ["#", "Even hashes (#) as keys are allowed"], ]).

item.title: len
item.description: Returns the number of items in a dict. This function does not generate a change. Function dict.len() Arguments None Return value Returns the number of items in a dict. Example This code uses len() to return the number of items in a dict: dict([ [0, 'item 0'], [1, 'item 1'], ]).len(); Return value in JSON format 2

item.title: map
item.description: The function iterates over all items on a dict and returns a new list based on the results of a given callback function. Be aware that the order when iterating over a set, dict or a dict is not guaranteed. This function does not generate a change. Function dict.map(callback) Arguments Argument Type Description callback closure (required) Closure to execute on each key/value pair.

item.title: restriction
item.description: Returns the dictionary key and value restrictions as a list of two strings. The first element represents the key restriction, and the second represents the value restriction. A dict can only be restricted when defined as a property of a typed thing (see the example). This function does not generate a change. item.title: set
item.description: Sets an item in a dict. If the key already exists, the old value will be overwritten. This function generates a change. Function dict.set(name, value) Arguments Argument Type Description name uuid/int/str (required) The key of the item to set. value any (required) The value to assign to the key. Return value The value that was set. Example This code shows how to use set():

item.title: values
item.description: Returns a list containing all the values of the dict. The order of values in the list is not guaranteed and may be different each time you run the query. This function does not generate a change. Function dict.values() Arguments None Return value Returns a list with the values of a dict. Example This code shows how to use values(): dict([ [uuid("00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"), 'UUIDs can be used as keys'], [-1, 'Integer keys can be negative'], ["#", "Even hashes (#) as keys are allowed"], ]).
